Since you’ve been comparing a Fender Stratocaster and a Gibson Les Paul, here are the main things to check at the store:

- **Play both through an amp similar to yours.** The Strat will feel brighter/snappier and more versatile; the Les Paul will feel warmer, fuller, and more sustain-heavy.
- **Check comfort and weight.** Strats are usually lighter (~7–8 lbs) and contoured; Les Pauls are heavier (~9–10 lbs) with a more angular body and often a thicker neck.
- **Pay attention to the neck and scale length.** Strat: 25.5" scale, bolt-on maple neck. Les Paul: 24.75" scale, set-in mahogany neck. See which feels more natural for chords, bends, and fingerpicking.
- **Match pickups to your style.** Single-coils for brighter, articulate tones; humbuckers for warmer rock/blues/metal tones. If you want flexibility, try a Les Paul with **coil-tap/coil-splitting**—models like the Les Paul Standard, Traditional, or Custom may offer it.
- **Test the styles you actually play.** If you care about acoustic-like fingerpicking, try that on the Les Paul—it can work, but its humbuckers, sustain, action, and wider neck may make it less ideal than a Strat or acoustic.
- **If you plan to use open D tuning, check setup.** Heavier strings, action/intonation, and pickup height matter; also try the neck pickup for a warmer tone.
- **Check the setup and intonation**, and compare prices: American Strats often start around $600–$800; American Les Pauls around $1,000–$1,500.

Bottom line: try several guitars, don’t rush, and pick the one that feels and sounds most like “home” for your playing style.
